provider.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1714-1715. The standard factory matches only the exact id 'sarvam' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:457), so a session that uses an alias falls to the flat factory. default_model records what the code does today: an empty model becomes saarika:v2.5 (gateway/src/core/stt/sarvam/config.rs:26, 141-145). That id is deprecated and absent from the legacy socket's documented model list; the audit recommends changing the default to saaras:v4, and this field must change in the same commit. Sarvam has two generations of socket: the legacy one the gateway speaks (one final per utterance, no interim text) and a realtime one with partial transcripts and manual endpointing, for which the gateway has no client. No Sarvam model on sale is file-only, so file upload is a fallback. Rate limits, not price, bind a segmented path here: 60 requests per minute per account on the Starter tier. The streaming client accepts only 8 kHz and 16 kHz sessions (gateway/src/core/stt/sarvam/config.rs:317-322), so a /v1/realtime voice agent, whose speech-to-text leg is set to 24 kHz (gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:342), fails at setup with Sarvam today. The rows list two commit transports that no release builds, the realtime socket and a gateway-driven flush on the legacy socket. Both carry the adapter id planned_commit and are told apart by dialect.wire (sarvam_realtime_websocket and sarvam_legacy_websocket), because they differ in wire format and language notation.

context_params.note: saaras:v4 only. At most 50 terms of at most 64 characters each, sent as one JSON-encoded array in a single field. Today's client does not send key terms on this socket; it appends a prompt parameter the legacy socket does not document (config.rs:276-279).

gateway_client.notes: The client has a mock end-to-end test and was verified live against this socket on 2026-06-04, but with the model saarika:v2.5, never with saaras:v4, so this row is recorded as wire-tested only. The vendor accepts keyterms for this model on this socket; the existing client does not send them, and instead appends a prompt parameter the legacy socket does not document (config.rs:276-279). This client dials the socket Sarvam now labels legacy (wss://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text/ws, config.rs:23). It returns one final transcript per utterance and no interim text. Each caller chunk is base64-encoded and sent at once as a JSON text frame (provider.rs:218-241); Sarvam's server-side voice detector ends the utterance; the gateway never sends a flush (flush_signal is fixed to false, config.rs:163). Differences from the vendor documentation, found by reading and not re-probed: the client matches voice-activity events named START and END while the vendor reference names them START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech (provider.rs:429, 447-460); the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:150-157); confidence is invented as 0.95 because the vendor sends none (provider.rs:430); finals are dropped if a 256-slot channel is full (provider.rs:433-444, 549); only 11 language codes are accepted and an empty language becomes hi-IN (config.rs:41-53, 146-150, 324-330); the codec check accepts 'pcm', which is not a vendor value, and rejects mu-law and A-law before any dial (config.rs:156-160, 333); no model id is checked (config.rs:315-346). The standard factory matches only the exact provider id 'sarvam' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:457). No vendor quality signal reaches the gateway on this transport, so none is listed. Sarvam returns language_probability on this socket only when it detects the language itself; this client cannot ask for that (an empty language becomes hi-IN, config.rs:146-150, and 'unknown' fails the language check, config.rs:41-53, 325-330), has no field for it in its response type (provider.rs:120-135), and reports a confidence that is the constant 0.95 (provider.rs:430). Validation rejects any session sample rate other than 8000 or 16000 Hz (config.rs:317-322). The /v1/realtime cascade sets the speech-to-text rate to 24000 (gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:34, 342), so a voice-agent session on that route, and any session at 24 kHz or 48 kHz, fails at setup on this transport. For an 8 kHz session the client writes 8000 into every audio frame (provider.rs:544); the vendor reference lists 16000, 22050 and 24000 for that field and says 8 kHz is set only on the connection, while the vendor's guide says to set it in both places, so the outcome for a telephone leg is unknown. The vendor's best-practices page says this socket closes after 60 seconds of inactivity and recommends silent audio as keep-alive. The client instead sends a JSON ping after 30 seconds without audio (config.rs:32; provider.rs:291-312), which is not a client message the vendor documents for this socket, and it treats any vendor error frame as fatal with no reconnect (provider.rs:254-260).
gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, not re-probed: voice-activity events are matched as START and END while the vendor sends START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech, and the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:429, 447-460, 150-157). Validation accepts only 8 kHz and 16 kHz linear PCM and 11 languages, so a 24 kHz /v1/realtime voice agent or a mu-law telephone leg fails at setup (config.rs:317-322, 324-333).

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. The realtime socket sends partial transcripts while the caller speaks and offers endpointing=manual, where the client sends speech_start, speech_end and flush; with endpointing=vad the vendor's own detector ends the utterance instead, which is why the owner is 'either'. gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text, multipart/form-data, file part named 'file', header api-subscription-key (an invalid key returns 403, not 401). Audio longer than 30 seconds returns 422, so the 25 second default segment plus padding must be checked against that cap before upload. The limit recorded, 60 requests per minute, is the Starter tier (Pro 100, Business 4,000); it is shared by every call on the Sarvam account across all keys, so a limiter above the per-session cap of two uploads is required. Retry only on 429, 500 and 503. The response has no transcript confidence, no no-speech probability and no word timestamps; an empty transcript is the only no-speech signal, and language_probability is present only when the language was auto-detected. WAV is detected automatically and is the vendor's recommended format; raw PCM needs input_audio_codec and must be 16 kHz. The vendor also accepts AMR and WMA, which the map's format list cannot name. Sarvam's batch job API (POST /speech-to-text/job/v1, then upload, start, poll, download) is answered in minutes and is not a live transport, so it is not listed. keyterms: up to 50 terms of at most 64 characters each, sent as one JSON-encoded array in a single form field, this model only.

The vendor's best-practices page says this socket closes after 60 seconds of inactivity and recommends silent audio as keep-alive. The client instead sends a JSON ping after 30 seconds without audio (config.rs:32; provider.rs:291-312), which is not a client message the vendor documents for this socket, and it treats any vendor error frame as fatal with no reconnect (provider.rs:254-260).

provenance.notes: Default for a Sarvam model id the map has never seen. The existing legacy-socket client is listed first, as on every Sarvam row with a working streaming client, so such a session gets what it gets today. Sarvam's synchronous file endpoint is listed behind it as a fallback, but no release builds a Sarvam file transcriber, so that transport is never enabled. The resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. The one known id for which this guess would be wrong, the socket-only saaras:v3-realtime, has its own row.
